children: The Canadian dollar strengthened to an 11-day high against its US counterpart on Tuesday, as investors raised bets on a Bank of Canada interest rate hike next month following a speech by the central bank's governor, Tiff Macklem.
was trading 0.6% higher at 1.42715 per US dollar, or 70.07 US cents, after touching its strongest intraday level since November 13 at 1.42665.

The Bank of Canada looks through temporary supply shocks but may need to respond sooner or more forcefully if shocks are large and persistent, demand is strong or there are expectations of persistent higher inflation, the central bank said.

"Taken together with recent research and statements from Macklem and his colleagues, it seems clear that officials are overwhelmingly convinced of an imminent inflation threat and see the balance of risks favouring pre-emptive action," Karl Schamotta, chief market strategist at Corpay, said in a note.

"This should help narrow (interest) rate differentials against the US dollar, but a material move in the loonie will likely have to wait for a decisive shift in the narrative surrounding America's growth trajectory," Schamotta said.

Investors see a roughly 80% chance the BoC will raise rates on December 9, up from 65% before Macklem's speech. Last month, the central bank lifted its benchmark rate by 25 basis points to 2.50%, its first hike in three years
The price of oil, one of Canada's major exports, rose as new attacks were reported on vessels in and around the Strait of Hormuz
were trading 2.1% higher at $81.81 a barrel, while the US dollar gave back some recent gains against a basket of major currencies.
Canadian bond yields were mixed across a flatter curve, with the 2-year (CA2YT=RR) up 2 basis points at 3.235%.
